name: cand_choice_rating
summary: Listener forced choice followed by a 5-point likelihood rating of a probed object.

charter.question: How do people jointly select a referent and grade the plausibility of alternative candidate referents across unambiguous, ambiguous, and uninformative messages?

instructions.welcome: Welcome to our study on how people understand descriptions of objects.
instructions.task: In each round, you will see a row of objects (such as robots, houses, or cupcakes) that differ in their parts. A speaker sees the same objects and wants to point out one of them. On most rounds, the speaker says a single word that is true of the object they mean. On some rounds, you have not heard the speaker's word yet. Each round has two quick parts: First, click the object you think the speaker is referring to. Second, one object will be highlighted with an orange frame, and you will rate from 1 (definitely not this one) to 5 (definitely this one) how likely it is that the speaker meant that highlighted object.

comprehension_checks.question: What do you do in the two steps of each round?
options: First pick the object you think the speaker meant, then rate how likely it is that the speaker meant the highlighted object.
Memorize the objects and redraw them from memory.
Pick every object that has the named part.

comprehension_checks.question: When the speaker says a word, what is true of the object they mean?
options: The object they mean always has the part named by that word.
The speaker says a random word that might not match their object.
The speaker is trying to trick you.
